hypothesis: The permanent short control made money during declines and lost during rallies. Test one downside breakout with a fixed risk budget and a protective buy stop; do not tune the channel or stop lengths. Compare against a permanent short using the same market opens and settlement clocks.
portfolio: Each 26-week account starts at 1000 USDT. Budget 20% gross per market and at most 0.5% of current equity per proposed trade for modelled stop distance. No borrowing, average-down or adding to positions.
signal: At daily open use the candle from two days earlier; enter short only if its close is below the lowest low of the preceding 20 complete days. Protective stop initially entry plus twice the average 14-day true range calculated through signal day. Tighten every following day to min(existing stop, highest high of the last ten completed days). Never widen. Only one position per market. No same-day re-entry.
execution: Use public perpetual daily OHLC and all observed eight-hour realized funding. Charge 0.10% adverse execution and 0.06% taker fee on every side; floor size to lot step. Buy stop fills at its level or at a worse opening gap; charge both costs. For ambiguous intraday stop timing charge every adverse intraday funding payment and credit none of the positive payments. Midnight funding on a carried position precedes any actions at its open. Cap entry size using both planned round-trip costs and stop movement, with no guarantee against gaps. Include cash weeks, terminal liquidation and 10% stressed maintenance.
evaluation: The oldest 26-week window was not used in the prior five-block short comparison. Require positive net and improvement over cash and the matching permanent short in both the oldest and most recent windows, lower drawdown than the control and at least 8 closed trades per window before considering a prospective strategy. Show all 6 blocks even if it fails. No automatic deployment and no parameter sweep.
